title: Continuation: stale carried blocks, ref sources, parent condition
range: git diff db8076a~1 db8076a (7 files, +134 -14) in the checkout trial/repo, saved as review.diff; files read at db8076a (detached HEAD), not a working tree. Places cited are at db8076a unless marked (base).

change.goal: A continuation stops carrying a kept block whose unit or a unit it uses changed, drops requirement sources that pointed into the previous record, and offers earlier answers to a conditional question only under the same parent condition.
change.why: An external review of PR 109 showed a consumer carried and kept though its unit had changed, a carried requirement's ref naming another entry, and an answer offered under a changed parent condition.
parts: staleCarried (review.mjs): one rule for which carried blocks cannot stand, called by carry and by check
carry (report.mjs): demotes stale blocks until none is left, judges their units again, drops ref sources and reports them
itemReads (page.mjs): a question reads with its parent's question and variants
three tests, a browser fixture edit, the data contract and the CHANGELOG

verdict:
The change does its task.
- the three rules behave as the commit says on the cases its tests assert: the report suite passes, 45 of 45, at db8076a
- one non-blocking design finding: the rule's fixed point lives in carry's loop, while check runs the rule once
- the rule's two other branches (a unit reached through two or more `uses`, a block with no unit) have no test in the suite that was run
- one open choice: whether a unit holding a block the previous record did not keep makes its kept blocks read again
now: staleCarried (review.mjs) returns a reason per carried block of an affected unit or of a unit-less block in a touched file. carry (report.mjs) calls it in a loop, drops each reported block's carried mark and verdict, then blanks the units with a block read again. check calls it once and refuses what it reports. carry drops ref sources of requirements and says which. itemReads reads a question with its parent's question text and variants.
target: The same behavior with the fixed point inside staleCarried: it treats every block it reports as not carried and repeats until none is added, so carry demotes from one call and check reports every stale block in one run. Two more tests (a two-step uses chain, a unit-less block in a touched file). The rest as written.
recommendation: Fix in place: move the repetition into staleCarried and add the two tests; answer question 1; accept the rest.

findings.title: The rule's fixed point is in carry's loop, so check reports a stale record in waves
findings.what: staleCarried is one pass: a block counts as touching its file only if it is not marked carried (review.mjs:173). carry repeats the pass, demoting what it reports, until nothing is reported (report.mjs:204-208). check calls it once (review.mjs:548). On a record where block A (unit stale) and block B (no unit, same file, no other block read again) are both marked carried, check reports A; B is reported only after A is fixed and check is run again. The rule is the same in name and owned in two places, against 'each fact has one owner'. Non-blocking: carry never writes such a record, only a hand-edited one meets the waves.
findings.shown_by: report.mjs:204 `for (let again = true; again;) {` against review.mjs:548 `staleCarried(review, files, owner, prev).forEach(`; review.mjs:173 `const touched = new Set(review.blocks.filter((b) => b.carried !== true)`
findings.fix: Do the repetition inside staleCarried (a block it reports counts as not carried in the next round, until no block is added) and let carry demote once from the one call.

findings.title: No test fails if the uses chain stops at one step or the unit-less branch goes
findings.what: Test 1 has one consumer using the changed unit directly. The loop `for (let grew = true; grew;)` that spreads through `uses` 'at any remove', and the `it has no unit` branch, are not asserted by any test in the report suite; the no-unit case is only exercised as a carried block that stays accepted, in the browser fixture (not run).
findings.shown_by: review-report.test.mjs:293-304 (units total uses rate, nothing deeper, every block has a unit); review-page-browser.test.mjs:71-72
findings.fix: Add a three-unit chain (c uses a uses the changed b) asserting c is read again, and a unit-less block next to a block read again asserting it is refused as carried.

blocks.does: CHANGELOG, Review report: says a kept block is carried only while its unit and the units it uses stand, that such a unit is judged again and that check refuses a stale block marked carried. It is the user-facing statement of the first rule of the task.
CHANGELOG: says a requirement source that pointed into the previous record by ref is left out and cited again. Statement of the second rule.
CHANGELOG: the answers offered back to an unchanged item now include, for a question, the parent's condition. Statement of the third rule; the rest of the lines is re-wrapped.

The browser suite's continuation fixture carried its first block with a unit that also holds a block not kept; under the new rule that block would be read again, so the fixture drops the block's unit and is carried by its file. It bends the fixture around the rule rather than testing it, and rests on how a unit holding a not-kept block counts (question 1).
Test helper: lays a previous record and diff under previous/, scaffolds the new diff, runs carry and returns its output and the record. Shared by the two carry tests.
Test fixtures: a two-file change (b.js's rate, a.js's total using it) as a diff for rate 2 and 3, and a record builder with units total and rate. Shared by the two carry tests.

Test 1: the next revision changes only the rate; the consumer block of total must come back read again (not carried, verdict blank, description kept), both units judged again, and a record marking it carried by hand is refused by check with the unit's name.
Test 2: a carried requirement whose only source was a ref into the previous record comes without sources, carry's output names it, and check refuses it as having no source.
Test 3: render of a revised record whose child question's parent variants changed: the earlier answers are offered to the parent (q3) and not to the child (q4).

Data contract, next revision: a carried block is kept for the code around it too; a block of a changed unit, of a unit that uses one, or with no unit in a file holding a block read again is read again and its unit judged again. Replaces the weaker sentence that only said to read a block with the change that touched its file.
Data contract: carry leaves out a requirement source that pointed into the previous record by ref and says so; a requirement left with no source is cited again.
Data contract: the answers offered back to a conditional question need the same parent and variants.

itemReads, the text an item is compared by across records: a question now includes its parent's question text and the variants listed, in place of dropping the parent. A child answered under one parent condition is no longer paired with the same child under another.
Imports staleCarried from review.mjs so carry uses the rule check uses.
carry copies the previous units as they were; the blanking of units not kept moves to the end of carry, after the stale blocks are known.
carry copies the previous requirements, leaving out each source that is a ref, since a ref into the previous record would name another entry here, and lists the ids that lost one.

carry asks staleCarried which carried blocks cannot stand and drops the carried mark and the verdict of each, repeating until none is reported. The repetition is needed because a demoted block can make its file touched. check does not repeat (finding 1).
carry judges a unit again, verdict and reason blank, when it has a block read again or a previous block with no carried counterpart; the units not kept and existing ones are treated as before.
carry counts the blocks that stayed carried after the demotion, and returns the ids of requirements that lost sources, for its message.
carry's message says some kept blocks are read again for a unit or file that changed, and names the requirements that lost sources and must be cited again.

staleCarried: for the record's carried blocks, finds the units whose previous blocks are not all carried or whose current blocks are not carried, spreads that through `uses` to the units that depend on them, and returns a reason for each carried block of an affected unit or of no unit in a file holding a block read again. It is the rule the task asks for, owned once and called by carry and by check.
check refuses each carried block staleCarried reports, with the reason and the way out.

challenges.point: carry no longer blanks the units not kept at the copy (the `unjudged` helper is gone), so a previous question or fix unit might come over judged.
challenges.note: the units are blanked at the end instead: `review.units = review.units.map((u) => u.existing || (u.verdict === "keep" && !reread.has(u.name)) ? u : { ...u, verdict: "", reason: "" });` keeps only a kept unit with nothing read again, and existing ones.

challenges.point: check might refuse a record carry has just written, because carry judges staleness before the units are blanked.
challenges.note: carry's loop ends only when `again = stale.some(Boolean);` is false, and the units are blanked after it, which staleCarried does not read (it reads `uses` only), so the call check makes returns none for that record.

questions.text: Should a unit that holds a block the previous record did not keep make its kept blocks read again?

context.text: staleCarried counts a unit as changed when any previous block of it is not kept, though its lines are unchanged.
The data contract says 'a block of it read again, changed or gone'; it does not say that a block not kept counts.

sources.quote: a block of it read again, changed or gone

context.text: The browser suite's continuation fixture was edited to drop the unit of its first block because of this.
No comparison outside the project was made.

variants.text: Yes, as written: an open block makes the unit's kept blocks read again.

consequences.text: A continuation never carries the kept blocks of a unit that still has a fix or a question; they are re-read with the open block.
The contract's sentence names the case; the fixture edit stays.

variants.text: No: only a block whose lines changed or are gone counts.

consequences.text: The `b.verdict === "keep" &&` test leaves staleCarried; kept blocks stay carried beside an open block, though its fix may change the code around them.
The browser fixture's edit is undone.

recommendation.text: Keep as written, and name the case in the contract: the fix of the open block changes the code around a kept block, which is what the rule asks to read again.
